A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including Appendix E added in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original language-model and image-classification experiments, including validation performance and optimizer-step reductions.

after.justification: v2 retains original training results and reports additional comparisons, tolerance-sensitivity results, and measured GNS-estimation overhead.

M1.justification: The GNS definitions, variance estimators, and Algorithm 1 retain the same adaptive-batching procedure, including moving averages, monotonic batch growth, and square-root learning-rate scaling. New Algorithms 2–3 document distributed implementations of the existing estimators.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4 language modeling with 160M and 1B Llama 3 models, Imagewoof classification with SimpleViT, and CIFAR-10 classification with ResNet-18. The added sensitivity and timing experiments reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Euclidean-GNS comparisons for Signum, AdamW, specSGD, and Muon, substantially extending the direct comparison central to the geometry claim. The signSGD Euclidean comparison already existed in v1 Table 9. Table 4 additionally evaluates NormalizedSGD.

E3.justification: The CIFAR-10 step-reduction reference changes from batch 512 to 256, and Table 7 expands tolerance, learning-rate, and momentum searches and revises initial-batch settings. Imagewoof gains a batch-512 control. Appendix E introduces timing experiments with specified local batches and 1,000-step measurements. These are substantive reported protocol changes and additions.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained initial-batch, learning-rate-scaling, and seed analyses, v2 adds a tolerance-sensitivity study at theta values 0.5, 0.6, and 0.7 in Table 10. New Appendix E investigates estimator overhead at two model scales and analyzes compute, communication, and memory costs, substantially expanding practical-efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: v2 replaces point estimates with plus/minus summaries and specifies 10 seeds for the 1B results and 5 seeds for CIFAR-10. Imagewoof results first specify 5 seeds; the 160M experiments already reported 10 seeds. Earlier unspecified run counts prevent inferring an actual increase in runs.

E6.justification: v2 retains the principal 160M non-Euclidean results but adds Euclidean entries and revises the 1B and vision results. For example, Table 3 replaces signSGD's adaptive loss of 2.8411 with 2.9946 ± 0.0201. New timing results report 0.2–0.3% overhead for l1 GNS and 13.9–39.9% for nuclear GNS. Revised CIFAR-10 percentages use different reference batches and tuning, so they are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Theorems A.4–A.5 add O(1/K) bounds on averaged squared dual-gradient norms under gradient-scaled learning rates without requiring strong convexity, with corresponding proof extensions. Appendix B corrects the second derivative and inflection-point multiplier from 64/9 to 16/9. Appendix E adds complexity bounds. However, the revised A.4 telescoping line drops an expectation and incorrectly factors the quadratic penalty.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statement, and conclusion retain the same central claims: geometry-matched GNS metrics, distributed variance estimation, and adaptive batching that preserves validation quality while reducing optimizer steps. The headline approximately 66% reduction remains unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 qualifies benefits from all optimizers to most, and Appendix D.2 identifies the CIFAR-10 MSGD exception. Appendix E explains nuclear-GNS overhead and identifies remaining implementation optimizations. However, D.2 retains a now-stale claim that Muon gives the largest step reduction: Table 11 reports 72.14% for signSGD versus 68.16% for Muon.

D1.justification: Appendix E substantially expands implementation documentation with layerwise FSDP pseudocode, explicit distributed collectives, gradient reconstruction, buffer requirements, and cost breakdowns. It also specifies profiling hardware, local batch sizes, measurement frequency, and averaging duration. These disclosures make the existing estimators substantially easier to implement and assess.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ahn et al.'s Dion paper as the source for distributed-collective notation in Appendix E. Most other reference changes update publication metadata or correct attribution for existing works, including Mann/Brown, without changing the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 tightens introductory paragraphs, adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements, updates acknowledgements and bibliographic text, and appends the computational-cost section. The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact; the added scientific material does not constitute extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Several comparison tables gain columns or rows, and Tables 3–4 become full-width displays. v2 adds sensitivity, latency, and complexity tables plus two FSDP algorithm panels. Figure 1 has revised axis limits and geometric illustrations, while Figure 3 is relocated. These substantially expand and reorganize the evidence displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central geometry claim through broader Euclidean-GNS comparisons and improves empirical transparency through multi-seed reporting. Appendix E addresses previously unquantified implementation costs with measurements and detailed pseudocode, exposing meaningful nuclear-GNS overhead. The corrected CBS derivation also improves accuracy. These gains outweigh the localized new proof-editing error and stale CIFAR-10 commentary, although the timing measurements do not establish end-to-end training speedups.
